diagnoses.description: Date disambiguation failure: selection likely came from a secondary date-like token (or OCR-corrupted DATE label such as DATE→DATA) rather than the primary header Date field. Root cause is weak ranking/selection (e.g., first-match or frequency vote) when multiple plausible dates exist in header region.
diagnoses.evidence: Allowed feedback: 034.jpg date_correct=false while amount_correct=true; prediction date=2018-08-09. The image shows a clear header block with a labeled Date field near the top (dd/mm/yyyy) and other header-adjacent metadata. Prior history and source-run OCR snippets show label corruption (e.g., “Salesperson: Data: …”) creating competing labeled candidates; first-match extraction is brittle in this scenario.

locations.section: Field Extraction Heuristics (Receipts) / Date extraction (reduce false positives)

diagnoses.description: Total selection failure driven by OCR digit-flip outlier (102.00→702.00) on a TOTAL-like line. The pipeline over-trusted a corrupted high-priority keyword match or a “last TOTAL wins” heuristic instead of enforcing receipt-internal anchor consistency (Subtotal/Payment/Total incl).
diagnoses.evidence: Allowed feedback: 074.jpg amount_correct=false while date_correct=true; prediction total_amount=702.00. The receipt image contains multiple anchors around 102.00 (Subtotal, Total incl. of GST, Total Amt Rounded, Payment), while 702.00 is a classic OCR 1→7 digit flip. Source-run trace shows OCR variants can produce both values; robust selection must reject candidates contradicting multiple anchors even if they appear on a higher-priority keyword line.

diagnoses.description: Rounding precedence failure: receipt shows an inclusive total, a rounding adjustment, then a final payable TOTAL; the pipeline selected the pre-rounding value instead of the final total after rounding, causing an exact-match miss (often by 0.01).
diagnoses.evidence: Allowed feedback: 077.jpg amount_correct=false while date_correct=true; prediction total_amount=23.26. The image shows “Rounding Adj: -0.01” followed by bold “TOTAL: 23.25”, while an earlier line shows “Total (Inclusive of GST): 23.26”. This requires an unconditional precedence rule: if rounding adjustment exists and a later TOTAL exists, always take the later TOTAL.

diagnoses.description: Coupled extraction + schema failure: total_amount was emitted as an empty string instead of null. This receipt also contains an “Amount” column header that can incorrectly trigger split-line fallback to an item amount unless explicitly excluded; OCR may corrupt both the GRAND TOTAL keyword and decimal separator (e.g., 92:80).
diagnoses.evidence: Allowed feedback: 078.jpg amount_correct=false; prediction total_amount="" violates task requirement (must be null on failure). Source-run trace shows matching on the column header line “Description Qty Price Amount” and split-line fallback to an item amount; other OCR variants show “GrandTota.”/“GrandTotal.” and “92:80”, and a stronger OCR variant (3× upscale + PSM4) yields “Grand Total … 92.80”. Regardless of extraction outcome, empty string must be converted to null.
